claims.text: The target material is a Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy whose liquid free-energy differences must be explored.
Constrained DFT has been used to generate training data for Moment Tensor Potentials in multicomponent alloys.
Actively learned MTPs have been demonstrated in refractory multicomponent alloys.
The cited refractory-alloy workflow supports an uncertainty-driven loop that adds configurations where the MTP uncertainty is highest.
Including high-temperature, disordered, and liquid-like configurations in the MTP training set will capture the complex liquid structure.
An MTP-based free-energy perturbation scheme can replace standard thermodynamic integration for calculating solid–liquid free-energy differences.
Standard EAM potentials fail in multicomponent liquids because they cannot represent complex short-range order and chemical fluctuations.
MTPs use higher-order descriptors that can represent complex multicomponent interactions more accurately than EAM potentials.
Active learning minimizes the MTP training set by selecting only the most informative configurations.
Selecting informative liquid-like configurations bypasses the need for exhaustive thermodynamic integration over the full phase space.
The failure mode of TOR-TILD in multicomponent composition spaces is exponential growth in the sampling required to converge free-energy differences.
An MTP perturbation scheme will converge free-energy differences with fewer samples than TOR-TILD.
The accuracy of the perturbation scheme depends on the training set covering the relevant liquid-state configurations.
MTP applicability has been demonstrated for solid-state properties of refractory multicomponent alloys.
The MTP perturbation scheme will predict melting temperature within 50 K of a high-fidelity DFT benchmark.
The MTP perturbation scheme will predict the solid–liquid free-energy difference within 2 kJ/mol of a high-fidelity DFT benchmark.
The proposed scheme will reduce computational cost by a factor of 100–1000 relative to standard thermodynamic integration.
The proposed MTP will correctly reproduce liquid short-range order.
The proposed MTP will avoid amorphization artifacts associated with simpler potentials.
Training only on solid-like configurations can produce an apparent efficiency gain while giving an incorrect liquid structure.
